title: agentarch MCP allowlist
description: Which MCP servers this project trusts, which of their tools it accepts, and what those tool descriptions said when a human last reviewed them. An MCP server contributes tool descriptions the model treats as authoritative, so accepting a server implicitly is accepting instructions from a third party.

default.description: Only one legal value. An allowlist that defaults to allow is a list, not an allowlist.

version.description: An exact version. A floating tag means the server you reviewed and the server you run are different programs.

integrity.description: Subresource-integrity style digest of the package, where the ecosystem provides one.

trust.description: Where it came from. community means nobody you can call is accountable for it.

reviewer.description: A named person. Review is an act someone performed, not a state a file is in.

tools_allow.description: Exactly the tools this project accepts. Anything the server offers that is not listed is refused.

tool_description_sha256.description: Digest of each allowed tool's description as it read at review time. This is the defence against a rug pull: a server can serve a benign description during review and a hostile one afterwards, and nothing else in the protocol would notice. `agentarch mcp audit --probe` compares these against what the server currently serves.

env_allow.description: Environment variables passed through. Everything else is withheld — a server inheriting the full environment inherits every credential in it.

allOf.$comment: A server you actually run has to be pinned; one reached over a URL is pinned by the operator at the other end.
A community-trust server runs somewhere bounded. Nobody you can call is accountable for its contents.
